section_summary: This section opens with a detailed Department of Commerce report on mid-1941 United States trade with Japan, China, Hong Kong, and the Kwantung Leased Territory. Subsequent records concern coordination of American, British, and Netherlands East Indies restrictions on Japanese trade, especially petroleum, textiles, strategic metals, and cotton, alongside intelligence on Japan’s oil reserves and wartime industrial preparations. The closing documents address Universal Oil Products Company’s refusal to transfer refinery technology to Japan and investigations of possible shipments of cotton and contraband mercury to Japanese destinations.

subfiles.title: Trade of the United States with Japan, China, Hong Kong and Kwantung, June 1941 and Six Months Ending June 1941
subfiles.from: Department of Commerce, Far Eastern Unit
subfiles.about: Reports and interprets United States trade with Japan, China, Hong Kong, and Kwantung during June and the first half of 1941.
subfiles.summary: The report finds that American exports to Japan fell sharply, with shipments largely confined to cotton and petroleum, while imports from Japan rose because of speculative raw-silk purchases. It compares trade with China by Free, Shanghai, and occupied areas and supplies extensive commodity tables for Japan, China, Hong Kong, and Kwantung. The figures also document reduced exports of strategic metals and machinery to Japan and the effects of the Japanese blockade on Chinese imports.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Netherlands East Indies Trade Policy Toward Japan
subfiles.to: Dean Acheson and Department of State files
subfiles.about: Records Baron van Boetzelaer’s request for clarification of American trade restrictions and his account of proposed Netherlands East Indies measures against Japan.
subfiles.summary: Van Boetzelaer said the Netherlands wished to avoid adopting policies either more liberal or more restrictive than those eventually chosen by the United States. He summarized an August 4 memorandum proposing the freezing of Japanese funds, severe restrictions on strategic exports, reduced petroleum quotas, and coordination among the United States, Britain, and the Netherlands East Indies. The memorandum warned that a weak or gradually tightened embargo could encourage Japanese expansion and weaken Chinese resistance.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Netherlands East Indies Textile Import Needs
subfiles.to: Dean Acheson and Department of State files
subfiles.about: Discusses efforts to obtain American cotton textiles for the Netherlands East Indies as replacements for Japanese imports.
subfiles.summary: Riemens and van Boetzelaer say American textiles would strengthen the East Indies against Japan; C. K. Moser backs it but notes producers are busy domestically, proposing a State note for manufacturers and an industry conference.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Standard Vacuum Remittances and Netherlands East Indies Oil Shipment
subfiles.about: Relays a Foreign Funds Control conversation about Japanese remittances and financing for an oil shipment from the Netherlands East Indies to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Singer asks status of applications for a $557,000 Japanese remittance and $105,000 for an oil shipment; Treasury is considering both, and Indies authorities would license export if financing is approved.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Memorandum of Conversation on Netherlands East Indies Trade Policy Toward Japan
subfiles.to: Dean Acheson and Department of State files
subfiles.about: Provides a second, poorly reproduced copy of the September 18 conversation with Baron van Boetzelaer.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats the Netherlands request for clarity on American restrictions and the Governor-General’s suggested policy toward Japanese assets, strategic goods, and petroleum. It again emphasizes coordinated American, British, and Netherlands East Indies action and warns that a partial embargo could strengthen Japanese militarists and undermine resistance in China.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Netherlands East Indies Petroleum Policy
subfiles.to: Dean Acheson and Department of State files
subfiles.about: Records confirmation that the Netherlands East Indies was prepared to embargo petroleum exports to Japan if the United States adopted the same policy.
subfiles.summary: Van Boetzelaer says the Indies government is ready to stop petroleum exports under a parallel American embargo; the Governor-General's August 4 memorandum was personal, not official, and Loudon described it to Welles, Hornbeck and the Secretary.

subfiles.title: British Embassy Letter Enclosing Parliamentary Statements on Trade with Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of British parliamentary answers concerning trade with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hall sends Acheson statements made in Parliament on September 9 and 10, with copies to Treasury.

subfiles.title: Parliamentary Question on Anglo-Japanese Trade
subfiles.from: Mr. Foot, Minister of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Answers questions about a reported barter arrangement and British trade with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Foot denies any general barter arrangement, says frozen funds can't pay for new exports to Japan, and states no trade is taking place between the U.K. and Japan.

subfiles.title: Parliamentary Question on British Exports to Japan
subfiles.from: Sir A. Duncan, President of the Board of Trade
subfiles.about: States British policy on licenses and exports of war-useful materials to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Duncan says Japanese assets were frozen July 26, exports to the Japanese Empire licensed from August 15, with no licenses granted since and no munitions-useful materials exported in three months.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of British Parliamentary Statements
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of British parliamentary statements about trade with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Acheson thanked Hall for his October 1 letter. He specifically acknowledged the enclosed statements concerning trade with Japan.

subfiles.title: British Embassy Letter Correcting Report on Bolivian Tin Shipments
subfiles.about: Corrects an earlier letter about suspected shipments of Bolivian tin through Chile to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Marris notes the earlier letter failed to ask the U.S. to approach Bolivian authorities, corrects "Bolivian" to "Chilean" for a shipping line, and supplies a replacement.

subfiles.title: British Embassy Letter on Empire Exports to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports whether strategic commodities were being exported from British-controlled territories to Japan.
subfiles.summary: British Embassy: no recent or planned Empire exports of tin, rubber, Indian pig iron, Malayan lead and zinc, or petroleum to Japan; no decision yet on which imports are essential.

subfiles.title: FBI Letter on British Firms Supplying the Japanese Army in China
subfiles.about: Reports allegations that two British firms were supplying the Japanese Army in China.
subfiles.summary: FBI report alleges China Import and Export Lumber and Jardine and Madison won Japanese Army business despite lower Japanese bids, with large commissions paid to Army personnel; copies went to Army and Navy intelligence.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Suspicious Railway Car at Tampico
subfiles.about: Reports the inspection at Tampico of a suspicious railway car previously dispatched from Manzanillo.
subfiles.summary: Tampico telegram: customs found 88 flasks of mercury and 264 zinc slabs in a railway car; Collins doubts an illegal export was intended and thinks it was moved to evade Manzanillo investigation.

subfiles.title: Telegram Requesting Cotton-Export Information from Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Requests information about cotton exports from Argentina and related Paraguayan shipments after August 1.
subfiles.summary: Telegram asks Buenos Aires to report recent cotton exports relevant to Japan and China, including Paraguayan cotton via Argentina, for the Economic Defense Board.

subfiles.title: Follow-up Telegram to Buenos Aires on Cotton Shipments
subfiles.about: Sends a follow-up request concerning the outstanding report on cotton shipments.
subfiles.summary: Mostly illegible follow-up telegram to Buenos Aires pressing for the reply needed to complete the survey of cotton shipments to Japan and China.

subfiles.title: Rio de Janeiro Telegram on Brazilian Cotton Exports
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy, Rio de Janeiro, Jefferson Caffery
subfiles.about: Reports Brazilian cotton-export figures connected with shipments to Japan and Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Rio telegram, largely illegible, gives a metric-ton equivalent and cites an October 17 report; the data entered the Department's October 28 Economic Defense Board summary.

subfiles.title: Letter Summarizing Latin American Cotton Shipments to Japan and China
subfiles.about: Summarizes reported cotton exports from American republics to Japan and China since August 1.
subfiles.summary: Collado reports cotton data: Brazil exported to Japan and Shanghai, Peru sent 10,317 metric tons to Japan, El Salvador none, Mexico possibly 800 bales of linters; Argentina's reply is delayed and Paraguayan transit needs verification.

subfiles.title: Letter Reporting No Argentine Cotton Exports to Japan
subfiles.about: Supplies the delayed Argentine response on cotton exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Buenos Aires reports no Argentine cotton exports to Japan since August 1, supplementing Collado's October 28 summary.

subfiles.title: Lima Telegram on Peruvian Cotton Shipments to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports the quantity of Peruvian cotton shipped to Japan between August 1 and October 15.
subfiles.summary: The Cotton Chamber’s compilation placed shipments at approximately 10,317 metric tons. The figure answered the Department’s October 18 inquiry.

subfiles.title: San Salvador Telegram Reporting No Cotton Shipments
subfiles.about: Answers the Department’s inquiry about cotton shipments with a report that none had occurred.
subfiles.summary: Ellis telegraphs from San Salvador that there were no cotton shipments whatever.

subfiles.title: FBI Cover Letter Transmitting Intelligence on Japanese Industrial Preparedness
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Transmits an October 16 memorandum about Japanese government activities in industry and commerce.
subfiles.summary: FBI cover letter sends reliable-source intelligence on Japanese industrial preparedness, copied to Army and Navy intelligence.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese Petroleum, Industrial Capacity, and War Production
subfiles.about: Compiles intelligence on Japanese oil refining, fuel reserves, aluminum production, military manufacturing, and industrial shortages.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum describes petroleum storage at Tsingtao, Mitsubishi refinery equipment, government oil controls, and detailed sales and consumption quotas for gasoline, kerosene, lubricants, and fuel oil. It estimates that Japan retained roughly two years of peacetime fuel-oil reserves but faced deteriorating refinery and labor efficiency. Additional reports cover aluminum production at Hachinohe, conversion of a Tokyo vehicle factory to military production, Hakodate dockyard expansion, military reservation of asphalt, shortages of electric motors, and Army interference with commercial shipping.

subfiles.title: Asunción Telegram on Paraguayan Cotton in Transit
subfiles.about: Reports small shipments of Paraguayan cotton moving through Argentina to unidentified foreign destinations.
subfiles.summary: Asuncion: only small Paraguayan cotton shipments went to Barranqueras, Argentina, destinations undetermined; Buenos Aires asked to verify onward exports.

subfiles.title: Universal Oil Products Letter on Japanese Refinery-Technology Contracts and Litigation
subfiles.from: H. J. Halle, Universal Oil Products Company
subfiles.about: Explains Japanese licensing agreements and requests a definitive government position before Universal is compelled to supply refinery designs.
subfiles.summary: Halle encloses the 1928 Sekiguchi agreement and papers in Japan Gasoline's Delaware suit; demands concern a Mitsui Mining cracking plant, failure risks crippling damages, and Saneyoshi is en route to New York, so he wants the government's position promptly.

subfiles.title: Division of Controls Routing Memorandum on Halle Letter
subfiles.about: Requests guidance on the response to H. J. Halle’s letter.
subfiles.summary: Green forwards the Universal Oil Products matter and asks what reply should be made to Halle.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Universal Oil Products’ Request for State Department Backing
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Green and Department of State officials
subfiles.about: Records Halle’s request for formal State Department support in defending Japan Gasoline Company’s lawsuit.
subfiles.summary: Halle says Universal faces a possible ten-million-dollar claim for observing the moral embargo and wants assurance it can tell the court it acted at State's request; Moseley asks for facts in writing and records that Tidewater Associated Oil and Mitsubishi jointly own a Japanese refinery.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Export Controls for Refinery Plans and Technical Information
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Green and Department of State officials
subfiles.about: Records Halle’s effort to place refinery plans and technical information under statutory export control.
subfiles.summary: Halle urged the Department to include refinery designs, specifications, and technical information among controlled defense articles, thereby giving the moral embargo a legal basis. He expected Masao Saneyoshi to arrive in New York to press the damages suit and wanted assurance of departmental backing before then.

subfiles.title: Memorandum Summarizing Universal Oil Products’ Japanese Contracts
subfiles.about: Summarizes the two contracts underlying Japan Gasoline Company’s legal action against Universal Oil Products.
subfiles.summary: The 1928 contract covered motor-gasoline information and patents, ambiguous under the moral embargo; the 1938 iso-octane agreement clearly fell within the aviation-technology policy; Universal got $700,000 and withheld the rest, and the Japanese Embassy and Morishima raised it.

subfiles.title: Mexico Telegram on Cotton Shipments to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports official and private information on Mexican cotton exports to Japan since August 1.
subfiles.summary: Mexico telegram: official August statistics and private sources show no cotton exports to Japan after August 1, though one firm thinks about 800 bales of linters may have shipped.

subfiles.title: Despatch on Attempted Contraband Mercury Shipment from Manzanillo
subfiles.about: Reports further developments concerning a suspected attempt to place contraband mercury aboard the Japanese vessel Azuma Maru.
subfiles.summary: Manzanillo: a car consigned to Antonio Llorens, manifested as 61 drums of bronze, was reshipped to Tampico on October 9 amid customs errors, prompting notifications to the Embassy, Tampico consulate and Mexican authorities. Continues past page 400.
